newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-The Weekend in Australian Sport.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-The Weekend in Australian Sport.

text.p: CRICKET

SYDNEY - Victoria opener Matthew Elliott was fighting an apparently hopeless battle after Victoria collapsed to be 100 for five at the end of the third day of their Sheffield Shield match against New South Wales on Sunday.
New South Wales had set Victoria an unlikely victory target of 457 when captain Greg Matthews declared his side's second innings closed at 353 for eight.
Pace bowler Phil Alley and leg-spinner Stuart MacGill then put the issue beyond doubt when they both took two wickets to have Victoria in a precarious position going into Monday's final day of play.
Elliott, who was named on Sunday in an Australian XI to play West Indies in Hobart from next Friday, was the only Victorian batsman to offer any resistance and was 63 not out at the close of play.
Victoria lost four of their five wickets for 29 in a decisive evening session for New South Wales.
The imposing target set by New South Wales was made possible by a dashing unbeaten innings of 150 by Michael Bevan, who had been 58 not out overnight.
Bevan lashed the Victorian attack and was ably supported by Michael Slater with 69 after Australia captain Mark Taylot and all-rounder Steve Waugh both failed.
The stylish left-hander was also backed up with support from tail-enders Phil Emery and Anthony Stuart.
Victoria captain Shane Warne, who is battling to prove his fitness for test duty after finger surgery in May, bowled 25 overs without reward to finish with none for 75.
Warne, Australia's main strike bowler with 207 wickets in 44 tests, took the wickets of two tail-enders in the New South Wales first innings.
CRICKET

PERTH - West Indies beat Western Australia by nine wickets on the final day of a three day tour match on Sunday but were left with a string of worrying injuries ahead of the first test against Australia later this month.

Foremost among West Indies' injury concerns was a strained groin suffered by key fast bowler Curtly Ambrose, prompting fears West Indies could go into the start of the first test in Brisbane on November 22 with an understrength pace asttack.
Shivnarine Chanderpaul set up the win for the West Indians, their second from four matches on their tour of Australia, with an unbeaten 135 in the first innings.

Western Australia, who had made 293 for six declared in their first innings, collapsed to be all out for 170, leaving West Indies needing 26 runs to win. Adrian Griffith scored 23 not out after opening partner Robert Samuels fell to Sean Carey for a duck.
All-rounder Carl Hooper, who scored 84 in the first innings, took four West Australian wickets for 59 in the home side's second dig.
Western Australia trailed West Indies by 148 on the first innings and all hope of saving the match vanished when they lost six wickets for 17 runs in 43 balls just after tea.
Despite the ease of the win, West Indies were concerned by injuries to star batsman Brian Lara and wicketkeeper Junior Murray.
Lara, who did not play against Western Australia, and Murray are both nursing sore hamstrings.
Former West Indies captain Clive Lloyd told reporters many of the injuries to his key players were due to playing on hard Australian wickets.
"Once they get accustomed to harder pitches and outfields, they'll be fine," Lloyd said.
Ambrose, Murray and Lara are likely to miss West Indies' next match against a Northern Territory Invitation XI in Alice Springs on Tuesday.
CRICKET

SYDNEY - Fringe test batsman Michael Bevan's 150 not out for New South Wales in the Sheffield Shield match against Victoria came on the same day the left-hander was chosen in an Australian XI to play West Indies in a four-day match in Hobart from Friday.
Bevan and pace bowler Anthony Stuart were the only New South Wales players named in the Australian XI, which will be captained by Queensland's Stuart Law.
Stuart pressed his claims by taking a career-best five for 63 in Victoria's first innings.

Bevan's 150 included 16 fours and was scored from 245 deliversies to go with hsi first innings of 79. Both innings were timely ahead of Australia's first test against West Indies beginning in Brisbane on November 22.
"I know for a fact that I still have to prove something," Bevan told reporters.
"I'm comfortable, I think I'm a test player. I've been scoring consistently for about three years, with the exception of three Tests and a couple of Shield matches. I'm not doing too badly."

The Australian XI team is: Stuart Law (captain), Michael Bevan, Andrew Bichel, Greg Blewett, Matthew Elliott, Adam Gilchrist, Jason Gillespie, Matthew Hayden, Brad Hogg, Darren Lehamann, Anthony Stuart.
CRICKET
ADELAIDE - England A lost seven wickets for 29 runs to be all out for 151 on Sunday in the second innings of their match against South Australia.
South Australia resumed at 232 for six and went on to make 276 before England A began their second innings with a lead of 18 runs.
In their second innings South Australia reached six without loss and need to score another 164 runs to win on Monday's final day of play.
Leg-spinner Peter McIntyre was the chief destroyer for South Australia, taking four wickets for five runs in the space of 21 balls. McIntyre finished with four for 43 from 22 overs.
South Australia captain Jamie Siddons took four catches, three of them from McIntyre's bowling.
Captain Adam Hollioke top-scored for England A with 28, while Michael Vaughan and Owais Shah both contributed 27. Greg Blewett and Ben Johnson were the not out batsmen for South Australia.
CRICKET
BRISBANE - A dashing innings of 76 by Tasmania batsman Michael DiVenuto was not enough to save his side from a 40-run defeat by Queensland in a Mercantile Mutual limited overs match on Sunday.
Queensland hit 275 for five, with Jimmy Maher hitting 91 and Geoff Foley 46 from 234 deliveries.
DiVenuto matched the aggression of Maher and Foley as he hit 78 from 57 balls, including 13 fours. DiVenuto brought his half century up off only 35 delieveries, the fastest this season.
Unfortunately DiVenuto was run out in the 15th over after batting partner Ricky Ponting failed to respond to a call for a single.
Ponting was eventually out for 46 with the score on 199 for six and all hope of an unlikely win for Tasmania gone.
The win put Queensland on top of the Mercantile Mutual standings with six points from three wins out of four matches.
Queensland's limited overs win came a day after they routed Tasmania by nine wickets in the Sheffield Shield after resuming on Saturday on one for no wicket at the Gabba.
Requiring 101 in their second innings, the home side cruised to victory with opener Trevor Barsby unbeaten on 48.
Queensland scored 244 in their first innings and dismissed Tasmania for 168 and 176.
RUGBY UNION

EDINBURGH - A personal kicking haul of 19 points from full-back Matt Burke hoisted Australia to a 29-19 victory over Scotland on Saturday to maintain his side's unbeaten record on their European tour.

The Wallabies never hit top gear in perfect conditions and were again indebted to Burke, who contributed 20 points in their recent 40-18 win over Italy, in an encounter which mostly failed to live up to expectations.
Australia led 19-6 at the interval thanks to four penalties and a conversion from Burke in addition to a close-range try from lock Warwick Waugh in the 14th minute.
Centre Daniel Herbert scored a second with 12 minutes to go, but despite second-half scores from wings Kenny Logan and Tony Stanger, the Scots were never close enough to mount a serious challenge.
Australian flanker Owen Finegan earned himself the dubious distinction of being the first player in international rugby to be substituted for reasons other than injury.
Following the recent law change by the International Board allowing tactical substitutions, he was replaced with 15 minutes left by ACT team mate Brett Robinson.
SOCCER

LONDON - Controversial Australian soccer player Mark Bosnich is likely to be out of action until Christmas because of slow progress made after recent knee surgery, the manager of his English Premier League club said on Saturday.
"We won't be pushing Mark too fast for his own good," manager Brian Little said.
A similar knee injury prevented Bosnich from making his first appearance this season until Villa met Tottenham on October 12, the day he made his now infamous Nazi salute to Spurs fans.

England's Football Association has not yet set a date to hear misconduct charges against Bosnich over the Nazi salute, which he said was based on the television character Basil Fawlty rather than Adolf Hitler.
A Scotland Yard investigation into the incident, which was the subject of a number of complaints to police, has also not been completed.
GOLF
MELBOURNE - Scotland's Catriona Matthew won the Australian Women's Open by three shots on Sunday after Corinne Dibnah of Queensland blew a four shot lead in the final round.
Dibnah had led from the start of the tournament but faltered with a dismal seven-over par 80 in the final round to plummet out of contention and finish fourth.
Matthew in contrast hit a final round of 69 for an aggregate of 283.
Australia's Karrie Webb fired her best round of the tournament, a 70, to finish second.
Defending champion Liselotte Neumann of Sweden was third.
